Subject: Annual planning: radical scenarios & staffing guardrails

Team —

Kickoff note for annual planning. I want us to intentionally bias toward clarity on two fronts this week: (1) scenario outcomes that materially change go/no-go funding bands (what I’m calling “radical scenarios”), and (2) simple, defensible staffing guardrails that product and hiring leaders can use while we iterate the FY27 plan.

What I’ve attached: a starting scenario matrix (2027_scenario_matrix_v1.xlsx) with three revenue/cost scenarios (Base / Stretch / Contingency) and a first-pass headcount sensitivity table. I also dropped a short markdown doc with proposed guardrails (staffing_guardrails.md).

Asks for this thread:
- Engineering (Jonas): confirm the three roadmap-influenced scenarios align with capacity and delivery risk — note any single points of failure that would push us to the Contingency row.
- Product (Markus): map the OKR alignment column in the matrix — call out features that are must-deliver vs. nice-to-have.
- Growth/Finance (Aditya): sanity-check revenue and CAC assumptions and suggest any alternative metrics we should surface to the execs.

Timing: please add comments in the Drive file by EOD Monday 4/5. I’ll synthesize for a 30m leadership pre-read on Tues 4/6, then a 60m cross-functional decision meeting on Wed 4/7 to lock on scenario thresholds and guardrails.

Finally, we will surface a short QBR prep checklist for each PM/Eng lead — that will be a separate doc but tied to the matrix outcomes.

Thanks — Laura

Laura — thanks for the clear framing. Quick reactions: 

- The three scenarios look directionally right. I noted two delivery risks that would force us into Contingency: (a) a critical transformer/kernel optimization not hitting perf targets, and (b) a multiregion rollout delay. I added comments in the Drive.
- For headcount, can we define the guardrail as a percentage delta from current FTEs (e.g., +/- 8%) rather than absolute slots? That keeps it flexible across teams.

Two asks back: 
1) Can Product call out which OKR outcomes require cross-team hires vs. reallocations? That materially changes our hiring runway math.
2) Can we surface one prioritized hiring freeze trigger (metric + threshold) for the Contingency scenario?

I’ll join the 4/7 meeting and prepare a short risk heatmap.

— Jonas

Hi Laura / team —

Thanks for including Acme Growth Partners and Stance Research on the kickoff. From an external planning/advisory lens, two quick items we typically recommend that might help the exec conversation: 

- Present three scenarios but highlight the likelihood and the operational triggers that move you between them (not just outcomes). That makes execs comfortable with an operational playbook.
- If you publish a staffing guardrail, tie a simple cost-to-impact ratio to each role bucket (e.g., platform infra hires vs. growth SDRs). It avoids debate in the QBR and surfaces priority hires quickly.

If useful, I can share a one-page template we use for QBR decks that maps scenario -> triggers -> immediate actions. Happy to drop that in the Drive.

Best,
